/* Returns the credit status and the numbers a credit controller looks at, false if the customer does not exist */
function GetCreditStatus($DebtorNo) {
	$SQL = "SELECT debtorsmaster.debtorno,
					debtorsmaster.name,
					debtorsmaster.currcode,
					debtorsmaster.creditlimit,
					debtorsmaster.holdreason,
					debtorsmaster.nextreviewdate,
					debtorsmaster.reviewmonths,
					debtorsmaster.exemptinterest,
					debtorsmaster.exemptfees,
					holdreasons.reasondescription,
					holdreasons.dissallowinvoices,
					currencies.rate,
					currencies.decimalplaces
				FROM debtorsmaster
				INNER JOIN holdreasons
					ON debtorsmaster.holdreason = holdreasons.reasoncode
				INNER JOIN currencies
					ON debtorsmaster.currcode = currencies.currabrev
				WHERE debtorsmaster.debtorno = '" . $DebtorNo . "'";
	$Result = DB_query($SQL);
	if (DB_num_rows($Result) == 0) {
		return false;
	}
	$Row = DB_fetch_array($Result);
	$Row['status'] = CCStatusFromHoldFlag($Row['dissallowinvoices']);
	$BalanceResult = DB_query("SELECT SUM(balance) AS balance FROM debtortrans WHERE debtorno='" . $DebtorNo . "'");
	$BalanceRow = DB_fetch_array($BalanceResult);
	$Row['balance'] = $BalanceRow['balance'] == '' ? 0 : $BalanceRow['balance'];
	return $Row;
}

changed is not counted against itself */
function CCCreditAvailable($DebtorNo, $ExcludeOrderNo = 0) {
	$SQL = "SELECT creditlimit FROM debtorsmaster WHERE debtorno='" . $DebtorNo . "'";
	$MyRow = DB_fetch_array(DB_query($SQL));
	$Available = $MyRow['creditlimit'];
	$SQL = "SELECT SUM(balance) AS balance FROM debtortrans WHERE debtorno='" . $DebtorNo . "'";
	$MyRow = DB_fetch_array(DB_query($SQL));
	$Available -= $MyRow['balance'];
	$SQL = "SELECT SUM(salesorderdetails.unitprice *
					(salesorderdetails.quantity - salesorderdetails.qtyinvoiced) *
					(1 - salesorderdetails.discountpercent)) AS ordervalue
			FROM salesorders
			INNER JOIN salesorderdetails
				ON salesorders.orderno = salesorderdetails.orderno
			WHERE salesorders.debtorno = '" . $DebtorNo . "'
				AND salesorderdetails.completed = 0
				AND salesorders.quotation = 0
				AND salesorders.orderno <> '" . (int)$ExcludeOrderNo . "'";
	$MyRow = DB_fetch_array(DB_query($SQL));
	$Available -= $MyRow['ordervalue'];
	return $Available;

function CCOrderCheck($DebtorNo, $OrderValue = 0, $ExcludeOrderNo = 0) {
	$Info = GetCreditStatus($DebtorNo);
	$Check = array('status' => 'normal', 'reason' => '', 'overlimit' => false, 'available' => 0, 'hold' => false);
	if ($Info === false) {
		return $Check;
	}
	$Check['status'] = $Info['status'];
	$Check['reason'] = $Info['reasondescription'];
	$Check['available'] = CCCreditAvailable($DebtorNo, $ExcludeOrderNo);
	if ($OrderValue > 0 AND $Check['available'] - $OrderValue < 0) {
		$Check['overlimit'] = true;

	$Info = GetCreditStatus($DebtorNo);
	if ($Info === false OR $Info['status'] == 'normal') {
		return '';
	}
	$Class = ($Info['status'] == 'stop') ? 'error' : 'warn';
	return prnMsg(CCStatusName($Info['status']) . ' - ' . $Info['reasondescription'] . '. ' . __('Credit limit') . ' ' . locale_number_format($Info['creditlimit'], 2) . ' ' . $Info['currcode'], $Class, '', true);
}

		return $Errors;

	$Errors[0] = 0; // None found.
	$Errors[1] = DB_fetch_array($Result);

	return $Errors;

   array of debtornos that fulfill this criteria.

	$Errors = array();
	$db = db($user, $password);
	if (gettype($db)=='integer') {
		$Errors[0]=NoAuthorisation;
		return $Errors;
	}

	$DebtorList = array(0);	    // First element: no errors

	}
	return $DebtorList;
}

input.new_string:
Credit Control

Credit control applies the same rules to every customer every time, and keeps a history of what was decided, by whom and when. It is built on the customer's credit status (the hold reason on the customer record) and credit limit. Only users who hold the Credit control security token (the credit controller, the deputy and the Finance Director) can change a customer's status or credit limit. Everyone else can look but not change - this includes sales reps and the sales office. The credit limit and credit status fields on the Customers page are ignored for anyone without the token.

Credit Reviews

Open Credit Control from the customer menu (or Accounts Receivable > Maintenance) and record a review: the outcome (limit confirmed, raised, reduced, put on watch, put on stop), the new credit limit, notes and the next review date. The limit changes at once and the review, with the notes, is added to the customer's history. Reviews cannot be changed or deleted. A new customer is given a next review date automatically when the account is opened, using the standard review period set in Credit Control Setup. A customer can be given a shorter review period of their own for higher risk accounts. The Credit Control Report lists the customers due or overdue for a review every time it is run.

Stop and Watch

A customer on stop cannot be supplied. No new order is accepted for them by any route - the sales office, the web shop, EDI orders, orders loaded through the API and standing (recurring) orders. Orders that were taken before the stop cannot be dispatched or invoiced either, unless credit control releases that order from the Credit Control Report. Web shop customers who are on stop are told that their account is on hold and to contact us. Put a customer on stop or take them off stop from the credit control page; a reason is always required and the change is recorded with the user and the date.

A customer on watch can still be supplied. Anyone taking an order for them is shown a warning, and their open orders are listed on the Credit Control Report. Watch status is not shown to the customer in the web shop.

For sales staff: a customer shown as on watch can still be sold to, but contact credit control first if you are worried. A customer shown as on stop cannot be sold to - do not try to work around it; contact credit control, who can take them off stop or release an order. Sales reps see the credit status, limit, balance and reminders of their own customers only.

An order that would take a customer over their credit limit is saved but held for credit control. It cannot be dispatched until credit control releases it from the Credit Control Report.

Disputed Invoices

Credit control can mark an open invoice as disputed on the credit control page. A disputed invoice is not chased and is not charged interest until the dispute is cleared. Notes about debt collection agencies or legal proceedings, which are handled outside webERP, can be added as a note against the customer from the same page.

Reminder Letters (Dunning)

Finance sets up the stages in Reminder Letter Stages: the number of stages, the days overdue that trigger each and the wording of each letter. The standard set is a polite reminder, a firmer second letter and a final notice. The reminder run (Accounts Receivable > Transactions > Credit Control Reminder Run) first shows who would get which letter. Untick the customers to leave out - for example where a payment has been promised - then send. Letters go by email to the customer's contacts that are flagged to receive statements, in the customer's own currency, listing the overdue invoices. Customers with no email address are listed and the letters are shown for printing and posting. A customer who has paid gets no letter, a customer is not sent the same stage twice in a short time, and disputed invoices are not chased. Every letter is recorded against the customer. After a final notice the customer is flagged for credit control to decide whether to put them on stop; webERP does not stop them automatically.

Month End Interest and Late Fees

Finance sets the annual interest rate, a flat late fee, the days overdue before a balance is charged and the income accounts in Credit Control Setup. At month end open Month End Interest and Late Fees, check the list of what will be charged to whom, untick anyone who should not be charged, and confirm. Interest is charged on overdue invoices only (not on earlier interest and fees unless Finance switches that on), pro rata for the days in the month. The late fee is charged once per customer per month. Charges are raised in the customer's own currency as separate items that appear on the customer account and on the next statement, and are posted to the general ledger. A month already charged for a customer cannot be charged again. Customers can be exempted from interest or fees on their credit control page. A charge can be waived with a reason, which also reverses it in the ledger.

Bad Debt Write-offs

Credit control can write off all or part of what a customer owes with a reason (Accounts Receivable > Transactions > Bad Debt Write-offs). Write-offs up to the amount set by Finance take effect at once. A larger write-off does nothing until the Finance Director approves it on the same page. A write-off reduces the customer's balance (it clears the oldest open invoices first), debits the bad debt account and credits the debtors control account, and puts the customer on stop unless credit control clears that option. If a written off customer pays later, enter the receipt in the normal way; the Bad Debt Write-off Report shows what has been paid since, and the accountant journals any recovery.

Credit Control Reports

The Credit Control Report lists customers due for a credit review, over their credit limit (and by how much, with totals in the company currency), on watch and on stop, and the orders held or taken for watched and stopped customers. It can be filtered by sales rep and currency. The Aged Debtors report shows each customer's credit status, limit and the last reminder stage sent. The Bad Debt Write-off Report lists write-offs over a period with who requested and approved them. The Debtors Ledger Reconciliation compares the total of the customer balances with the debtors control account in the general ledger and lists the transactions where they disagree. Customers who log in can see the reminders sent to them, the interest and fees charged and their balance under Reminders and Charges; they only ever see their own account.

Everyone else can look but not change - this includes sales reps and the sales office. The credit limit and credit status fields on the Customers page are ignored for anyone without the token.

Credit Reviews

Open Credit Control from the customer menu (or Accounts Receivable > Maintenance) and record a review: the outcome (limit confirmed, raised, reduced, put on watch, put on stop), the new credit limit, notes and the next review date. The limit changes at once and the review, with the notes, is added to the customer's history. Reviews cannot be changed or deleted. A new customer is given a next review date automatically when the account is opened, using the standard review period set in Credit Control Setup. A customer can be given a shorter review period of their own for higher risk accounts. The Credit Control Report lists the customers due or overdue for a review every time it is run.

Stop and Watch

A customer on stop cannot be supplied. No new order is accepted for them by any route - the sales office, the web shop, EDI orders, orders loaded through the API and standing (recurring) orders. Orders that were taken before the stop cannot be dispatched or invoiced either, unless credit control releases that order from the Credit Control Report. Web shop customers who are on stop are told that their account is on hold and to contact us. Put a customer on stop or take them off stop from the credit control page; a reason is always required and the change is recorded with the user and the date.

A customer on watch can still be supplied. Anyone taking an order for them is shown a warning, and their open orders are listed on the Credit Control Report. Watch status is not shown to the customer in the web shop.

For sales staff: a customer shown as on watch can still be sold to, but contact credit control first if you are worried. A customer shown as on stop cannot be sold to - do not try to work around it; contact credit control, who can take them off stop or release an order. Sales reps see the credit status, limit, balance and reminders of their own customers only.

An order that would take a customer over their credit limit is saved but held for credit control. It cannot be dispatched until credit control releases it from the Credit Control Report.

Disputed Invoices

Credit control can mark an open invoice as disputed on the credit control page. A disputed invoice is not chased and is not charged interest until the dispute is cleared. Notes about debt collection agencies or legal proceedings, which are handled outside webERP, can be added as a note against the customer from the same page.

Reminder Letters (Dunning)

Finance sets up the stages in Reminder Letter Stages: the number of stages, the days overdue that trigger each and the wording of each letter. The standard set is a polite reminder, a firmer second letter and a final notice. The reminder run (Accounts Receivable > Transactions > Credit Control Reminder Run) first shows who would get which letter. Untick the customers to leave out - for example where a payment has been promised - then send. Letters go by email to the customer's contacts that are flagged to receive statements, in the customer's own currency, listing the overdue invoices. Customers with no email address are listed and the letters are shown for printing and posting. A customer who has paid gets no letter, a customer is not sent the same stage twice in a short time, and disputed invoices are not chased. Every letter is recorded against the customer. After a final notice the customer is flagged for credit control to decide whether to put them on stop; webERP does not stop them automatically.

Month End Interest and Late Fees

Finance sets the annual interest rate, a flat late fee, the days overdue before a balance is charged and the income accounts in Credit Control Setup. At month end open Month End Interest and Late Fees, check the list of what will be charged to whom, untick anyone who should not be charged, and confirm. Interest is charged on overdue invoices only (not on earlier interest and fees unless Finance switches that on), pro rata for the days in the month. The late fee is charged once per customer per month. Charges are raised in the customer's own currency as separate items that appear on the customer account and on the next statement, and are posted to the general ledger. A month already charged for a customer cannot be charged again. Customers can be exempted from interest or fees on their credit control page. A charge can be waived with a reason, which also reverses it in the ledger.

Bad Debt Write-offs

Credit control can write off all or part of what a customer owes with a reason (Accounts Receivable > Transactions > Bad Debt Write-offs). Write-offs up to the amount set by Finance take effect at once. A larger write-off does nothing until the Finance Director approves it on the same page. A write-off reduces the customer's balance (it clears the oldest open invoices first), debits the bad debt account and credits the debtors control account, and puts the customer on stop unless credit control clears that option. If a written off customer pays later, enter the receipt in the normal way; the Bad Debt Write-off Report shows what has been paid since, and the accountant journals any recovery.

Credit Control Reports

The Credit Control Report lists customers due for a credit review, over their credit limit (and by how much, with totals in the company currency), on watch and on stop, and the orders held or taken for watched and stopped customers. It can be filtered by sales rep and currency. The Aged Debtors report shows each customer's credit status, limit and the last reminder stage sent. The Bad Debt Write-off Report lists write-offs over a period with who requested and approved them. The Debtors Ledger Reconciliation compares the total of the customer balances with the debtors control account in the general ledger and lists the transactions where they disagree. Customers who log in can see the reminders sent to them, the interest and fees charged and their balance under Reminders and Charges; they only ever see their own account.

Accounts Receivable

Overview

A primary function of the system is to track the amounts owed to the business by customers in both local and foreign currency. The system shows, invoice-by-invoice, the balance on the account and does not lose the detail of what makes the account up in a balance brought forward - it is an "open item" system. When payments received from customers are entered and allocated to invoices, the differences on exchange are calculated and posted to the general ledger - that is only if integration to the general ledger is enabled from the company preferences page under the setup tab.

Features

  • Overdues inquiry that takes into account delivery days to the customer's branch and the actual terms applicable to the customer, supported by detailed inquiry of actual invoices overdue.
  • Full on-screen inquiry on a customer's account, complete with invoice details and narrative which appeared on the invoice. Inquiries on payments received will show how a payment was allocated to invoices and the difference on exchange attributable to each invoice.
  • Full integration with stock records and general ledger -a full trail of journals for each transaction is maintained - a drill down to the general ledger transactions for each transaction on a customers account is available from the customer inquiry page.
  • Open item - full analysis of the outstanding balance is maintained and printed on statements for maximum information to the customer.
  • Flexible user definable sales analysis reports to pdf or spreadsheet (csv - comma separated values).
  • Retrospective - de-allocation and re-allocation of receipts or credit notes against charges with re-calculation of differences on exchange and corresponding general ledger journals
  • Any number of branch - delivery addresses can be added serviced by different sales people with different tax authorities and different areas for sales analysis purposes.
  • Unlimited free form notes can be maintained for each customer and an unlimited number of contacts can be stored against each customer>
  • Email of customer statements to multiple customer contacts
⬆ Top

Entering New Customers

From the menu Receivables tab, click on "Add A New Customer". The customer record is the actual charge account, any number of branches can be defined for each customer account. At least one branch must be defined for each customer. It is the branch details that record the local information about delivery address, tax authority, sales area and sales person.

Customer Code

This field is used as a unique identifier for the customer which is small (maximum of 10 characters of text - letters or numbers). This allows faster searches for customers and keeps the size of the database at a minimum.

Note: A customer code can be altered retrospectively but because of the large scale of the changes required to the system to update stock movement transactions, sales analysis records and sales orders it could present a significant drain on resources. The option to change a customer code is in the utility menu Z_index.php - which must be entered as a manual URL and is only accessible by the system administrator. Such changes should only be undertaken when there are no other users on the system.

Customer Name

The name of the customer is used extensively in lookups and appears on invoices and statements exactly as typed (searches are independent of case). Proper capitalisation and use of the full name of the customer is recommended. The maximum length of the name is 40 characters.

Address Line 1, 2, 3 and 4

This is the address of where invoices and statements are to be posted. A post office box should be entered if applicable. These fields will allow a maximum of 40 characters and are optional. If left out invoices will not show the customer's address which is a requirement for a valid GST or VAT invoice in some administrations.

Currency

This is a compulsory field that identifies the currency in which the customer is to be invoiced. All invoices created for the customer will use this currency and the rate will be used as set up in the currency master - accessible from the General Ledger module. The currency rates need to be maintained at least monthly.

Note: that the rate is recorded in the transaction not the currency. If a customer changes the currency in which they are invoiced it is possible to allocate a new currency receipt against invoices (invoiced in the old currency) in which case the system will calculate large differences on exchange. Note: There is no error check on this and care should be taken, should this occur, to ensure invoices are matched off in the currency in which they were originally created - the cross rate between the new and old currency will provide an equivalent amount of the old currency for entry and allocation.

Invoice Discount

Customers can be set up with a general level of discount which applies to all sales. The percentage entered is used by default on all invoices to the customer. The discount rate can be manually overridden at the time of invoicing, which the system will use to calculate discount. The discount percentage used at invoice time will not be stored as the future default unless the customer details are amended. This field checks to ensure that the percentage is less than 100% and greater or equal to zero. This feature is not currently used/implemented.

Prompt Payment Discount

Customers can be set up with individual prompt payment discount percentages. This field is for memorandum purposes only and shows on screen when customer receipts are entered. If the receipt is on time the discount can be calculated and input with the receipt.

Customer Since

The default is the current date. This field is only used on certain reports where it can be used to restrict the customers shown, and also for credit reference inquiries. The system will only accept a date in this field. The date can be altered at any time. There is no error checking on this field.

Payment Terms

A select box is provided showing the predefined payment terms. New ones can be created as necessary from the Setup tab of the menu. The terms are used to determine whether an account is overdue or not and a description of the terms prints out on invoices, and statements.

There are no restrictions on altering payment terms for a customer at any time. The next statement or invoice produced will show the new terms. The system will only look at the new terms in deciding whether or not invoices are overdue, no record of the terms is held in the transaction itself.

Credit Status or Rating

A lookup is available for this field and a button is available for creation of new credit status categories. Credit status's can be defined to stop any new invoices or indeed orders to the customer - irrespective of his/her credit limit.

A customers Credit Status can be altered at any time.

Note: This will never show on any reports invoices, credits or statement intended for the customers eyes.

Credit Limit

This is a required field which accepts any positive value. It is currently only for memorandum purposes.

Invoice Addressing

This field is a flag that has two choices:

  • To address invoices to the head office postal address. This is the postal address from the customer record as entered above. This is the default option.
  • To address invoices to the branch postal address. This addresses invoices charged to the customer to the branch of the customer, some customers may wish for the branch to authorise invoices before sending on to head office for payment. The branch postal address entered will be used for printing invoices.
⬆ Top

Entering Customer Branches

A customer code entered on its own is insufficient to enter sales orders against. All customers must have at least one branch. The branch records contain the information about the delivery address, the sales area, the tax code, the sales representative and other regional information. New branches can be set up at any time. The first step will always be to select the customer, then to Add/Edit/Delete Customer Branch Records from the Customer menu. There is no limit to the number of branches that can be referenced against a single charge account (customer record). However, branches cannot be transferred between different customers. Only one statement will print per customer, but each invoice will be referenced to the branch it was delivered to.

Branch Name

The branch name can be up to 40 characters long. The branch name is used on packing slips to identify the name to where delivery should be made. It is also used in lookups in sales order entry as it is to the branch that the sale is ordered against. By selecting the branch from this lookup, the customer code and branch code is returned to the system for storing against the order.

Branch Code

The branch code is stored in transactions. It can be up to 10 characters long and should uniquely identify the branch. Two branches cannot have the same code for the same customer. Branch codes (and other codes) cannot contain spaces, commas, & or - . There are checks in place to ensure no new codes are created containing these characters. However, if data is imported it is important to change any codes which contravene these rules.

Branch codes are not available for modification retrospectively. They exist in many tables throughout the database - sales analysis, orders, DebtorTrans and CustTrans and all data in these tables would need to be modified.

Branch Contact / Phone / Fax / Address

The branch contact is the name of the purchasing manager to whom goods and inquiries would be addressed at the branch. A head office branch could be created to identify contact names for account inquiries. It doesn't matter that such a branch may not be invoiced to.

The address is the physical address of the branch for deliveries. As much detail as is required on labels to get the goods to the desired destination should be entered.

Sales Person

A select box is available to enter the salesperson who services this branch.

Draw Stock From

Branches local to a particular warehouse can be associated with the local warehouse by setting this field to the preferred stocking location (see Inventory Locations Maintenance). This affects the entry of sales orders that default to the stock location entered here. It can be overridden at the time of order entry.

Forward Date From A Day In The Month

This field is not currently used.

Delivery Days

This field is not currently used.

Phone/Fax/Email

These are the contact details applicable to the branch.

Tax Authority

The tax authority of the branch determines the regime for tax calculations at invoice and credit time.

Tax Authorities are the authority that collects the taxes. Different authorities in different countries mainly or different states in the USA. Say sales tax in New York is 10% and sales to customers in Michigan attract sales tax at a different rate payable to a different state tax authority.

In the UK, Australia and NZ, the Inland Revenue, Australian Tax Office and the IRD are the relevant tax authorities. Sales to customers that fall under the ATO from a company in NZ do not attract any tax - ie exempt export. However, the same customer who has a branch in Auckland NZ will fall under a different tax authority the NZ IRD - attracting GST @ 12.5% for the same item delivered there.

So the tax authority is the factor relevant based on where the branch of the customer is who is receiving the supply.

The tax authorities are maintained in a separate table (available from the Setup tab) and the tax rate applicable to invoices and credits and the general ledger posting of tax is determined from the Tax Authority setting of the branch together with the applicable level of tax specified in the item (stock) master.

A select box allows the appropriate tax authority for the branch to be selected.

Disable Transactions

This flag - either enabled or disabled - either includes the branch as available for new sales orders or not. If it is set to disabled then the branch will not appear on the order entry branch lookup.

Default Freight Company

A select box allows the selection of the freight company that is most cost/service effective for deliveries to this branch. The entry in this field serves as the default for future sales orders. If it is changed at order entry stage, the overridden entry become the new entry for this field.

Postal Address 1, 2, 3 and 4

This is the postal address of the branch. There is no checking done to ensure this is entered. The only place this would be used is if the customer record required that invoices and credits be addressed to the branch.

⬆ Top

Amending Customer Details

The customer details can be modified at any time and any modifications made will be effective for all future transactions. First select the customer from the link provided on all pages, then select the link for Modify Customer Details.

Points to note:

  • Customer codes can be modified retrospectively using the facility in the utilities menu Z_index.php - this should be used only when all other users are off the system.
  • Changing the payment terms impacts immediately on the aged analysis since this is recalculated each time it is run or a statement is produced.
  • Changing the currency of the customer needs care since the exchange rate is recorded against each transaction. Allocations of one currency against another at different rates will produce differences on exchange. The system will not be able to distinguish at the transactions level which was in what currency only the rate against the functional currency.

Customer Statements

Customer statements can either be printed or emailed directly to all the customers in the selected range, that have a contact defined as receiving a statement. If there are no contacts defined for the customer that have the statement flag set to yes then their statement will not be emailed to them. If the customer has many contacts with several of them having the statement flag set to yes then all those contacts will receive a copy of the pdf statement.

If the customer has any contacts that have the statement flag set then it will not be possible to print their statement so as to avoid sending both a printed statement and an email statement

⬆ Top

Customer Notes

Customer notes containing any text - a web-link if required and a date can be entered from the Select Customer screen - for the selected customer. The notes are displayed in sequence of priority - so pressing issues appear at the top of the list. These notes might contain information about recent contact with the customer or disputes. There is no checking on the content of the notes and no limit to either the number of notes nor the number of characters that can be used.

Customer Type Notes

As well as unlimited notes on individual customers, webERP has the functionality to store an unlimited number of notes on groups of customers based on the debtor type field. As with the notes on individual customers , these notes are displayed in order of priority, and can contain a URL as well as the free form note.

Shippers

This table is only used as a reference to the method of transportation that the invoice delivery was effected by. The shippers name is what is used in the look ups and the code is a system maintained counter which is stored in the database to reference the freight company used. The consignment note reference can be stored against the transaction in the reference field. In this way a full proof of delivery trail can be maintained.

Shipment cost calculations can be automated and the result automatically added to invoices. The least cost shipper is calculated and modified on the order. This system requires active maintenance of the shipment costs tables for each shipper. The shipper costs table shows the cost per kg and metre cubed for freight to destination cities. A substantial amount of data is required. For the system to calculate freight, it also requires that each part have a defined volume and weight set up from which the total order weight and volume is determined for use in the freight calculations.

If freight cost calculations are to be performed at order entry stage, the data must be entered and the options in config.php enabled - see the config.php section.

<?php

/* Credit control shared functions.

Credit status is not stored in a column of its own. A customer's status comes from the hold reason on debtorsmaster, the
way the rest of webERP already reads it:
	holdreasons.dissallowinvoices = 1  customer is on stop
	holdreasons.dissallowinvoices = 2  customer is on watch
	anything else                      normal

Everything that changes credit control state writes a row to creditcontrollog so the history per customer can be audited.
*/

function CCSetting($Name, $Default = '') {
	return isset($_SESSION[$Name]) ? $_SESSION[$Name] : $Default;
}

/* Credit controller, deputy and Finance Director hold security token 21. Anyone else - reps, sales office, order entry - can look but not change */
function CCIsCreditController() {
	return isset($_SESSION['AllowedPageSecurityTokens']) AND in_array(21, $_SESSION['AllowedPageSecurityTokens']);
}

/* Only the Finance Director approves large write-offs - token 22 */
function CCIsFinanceDirector() {
	return in_array(22, $_SESSION['AllowedPageSecurityTokens']);
}

function CCStatusName($Status) {
	if ($Status == 'stop') {
		return __('On stop');
	} elseif ($Status == 'watch') {
		return __('On watch');
	}
	return __('Normal');
}

function CCStatusFromHoldFlag($DissallowInvoices) {
	if ($DissallowInvoices == 1) {
		return 'stop';
	} elseif ($DissallowInvoices == 2) {
		return 'watch';
	}
	return 'normal';
}

function CCWriteLog($DebtorNo, $Action, $Detail, $Amount = 0, $TransType = 0, $TransNo = 0) {
	/* the history is append only - nothing in webERP updates or deletes creditcontrollog rows */
	$SQL = "INSERT INTO creditcontrollog (debtorno,
										logdate,
										userid,
										action,
										detail,
										amount,
										transtype,
										transno)
					VALUES ('" . $DebtorNo . "',
							'" . date('Y-m-d H:i:s') . "',
							'" . $_SESSION['UserID'] . "',
							'" . $Action . "',
							'" . DB_escape_string(stripslashes($Detail)) . "',
							'" . $Amount . "',
							'" . $TransType . "',
							'" . $TransNo . "')";
	DB_query($SQL, __('The credit control history could not be recorded because'));
}

/* Returns the credit status and the numbers a credit controller looks at, false if the customer does not exist */
function GetCreditStatus($DebtorNo) {
	$SQL = "SELECT debtorsmaster.debtorno,
					debtorsmaster.name,
					debtorsmaster.currcode,
					debtorsmaster.creditlimit,
					debtorsmaster.holdreason,
					debtorsmaster.nextreviewdate,
					debtorsmaster.reviewmonths,
					debtorsmaster.exemptinterest,
					debtorsmaster.exemptfees,
					holdreasons.reasondescription,
					holdreasons.dissallowinvoices,
					currencies.rate,
					currencies.decimalplaces
				FROM debtorsmaster
				INNER JOIN holdreasons
					ON debtorsmaster.holdreason = holdreasons.reasoncode
				INNER JOIN currencies
					ON debtorsmaster.currcode = currencies.currabrev
				WHERE debtorsmaster.debtorno = '" . $DebtorNo . "'";
	$Result = DB_query($SQL);
	if (DB_num_rows($Result) == 0) {
		return false;
	}
	$Row = DB_fetch_array($Result);
	$Row['status'] = CCStatusFromHoldFlag($Row['dissallowinvoices']);
	$BalanceResult = DB_query("SELECT SUM(balance) AS balance FROM debtortrans WHERE debtorno='" . $DebtorNo . "'");
	$BalanceRow = DB_fetch_array($BalanceResult);
	$Row['balance'] = $BalanceRow['balance'] == '' ? 0 : $BalanceRow['balance'];
	return $Row;
}

/* Credit available to a customer. The same arithmetic as GetCreditAvailable() but it can leave one order out, so an order that is being
changed is not counted against itself */
function CCCreditAvailable($DebtorNo, $ExcludeOrderNo = 0) {
	$SQL = "SELECT creditlimit FROM debtorsmaster WHERE debtorno='" . $DebtorNo . "'";
	$MyRow = DB_fetch_array(DB_query($SQL));
	$Available = $MyRow['creditlimit'];
	$SQL = "SELECT SUM(balance) AS balance FROM debtortrans WHERE debtorno='" . $DebtorNo . "'";
	$MyRow = DB_fetch_array(DB_query($SQL));
	$Available -= $MyRow['balance'];
	$SQL = "SELECT SUM(salesorderdetails.unitprice *
					(salesorderdetails.quantity - salesorderdetails.qtyinvoiced) *
					(1 - salesorderdetails.discountpercent)) AS ordervalue
			FROM salesorders
			INNER JOIN salesorderdetails
				ON salesorders.orderno = salesorderdetails.orderno
			WHERE salesorders.debtorno = '" . $DebtorNo . "'
				AND salesorderdetails.completed = 0
				AND salesorders.quotation = 0
				AND salesorders.orderno <> '" . (int)$ExcludeOrderNo . "'";
	$MyRow = DB_fetch_array(DB_query($SQL));
	$Available -= $MyRow['ordervalue'];
	return $Available;
}

/* The one question every order route asks before it accepts an order: can this customer be supplied?

Returns an array: status (normal, watch, stop), reason (hold reason text), overlimit (true when the order takes the customer over their limit),
available (credit left before this order) and hold (true when the order must be held for credit control approval).
Stop is a refusal whatever the value. Over limit is a hold, unless CCHoldOverLimitOrders is switched off. */
function CCOrderCheck($DebtorNo, $OrderValue = 0, $ExcludeOrderNo = 0) {
	$Info = GetCreditStatus($DebtorNo);
	$Check = array('status' => 'normal', 'reason' => '', 'overlimit' => false, 'available' => 0, 'hold' => false);
	if ($Info === false) {
		return $Check;
	}
	$Check['status'] = $Info['status'];
	$Check['reason'] = $Info['reasondescription'];
	$Check['available'] = CCCreditAvailable($DebtorNo, $ExcludeOrderNo);
	if ($OrderValue > 0 AND $Check['available'] - $OrderValue < 0) {
		$Check['overlimit'] = true;
		if (CCSetting('CCHoldOverLimitOrders', 1) == 1) {
			$Check['hold'] = true;
		}
	}
	return $Check;
}

/* The value of an order the way GetCreditAvailable() values it - lines still to be invoiced, less discount */
function CCOrderValue($OrderNo) {
	$SQL = "SELECT SUM(unitprice * (quantity - qtyinvoiced) * (1 - discountpercent)) AS ordervalue
			FROM salesorderdetails
			WHERE orderno = '" . (int)$OrderNo . "'
				AND completed = 0";
	$MyRow = DB_fetch_array(DB_query($SQL));
	return $MyRow['ordervalue'] == '' ? 0 : $MyRow['ordervalue'];
}

/* Whether an order that already exists may be dispatched and invoiced. Returns '' when it may, otherwise the reason it may not.
A stop blocks every order taken before the stop unless credit control has released that order (creditheld = 2).
An order held for the credit limit stays blocked until released. */
function CCDispatchBlockReason($OrderNo) {
	$SQL = "SELECT salesorders.debtorno,
					salesorders.creditheld,
					salesorders.quotation
			FROM salesorders
			WHERE salesorders.orderno = '" . (int)$OrderNo . "'";
	$Result = DB_query($SQL);
	if (DB_num_rows($Result) == 0) {
		return '';
	}
	$Order = DB_fetch_array($Result);
	if ($Order['creditheld'] == 2) {
		return '';
	}
	if ($Order['creditheld'] == 1) {
		return __('This order is held for credit control approval because it takes the customer over their credit limit. It can be dispatched once credit control releases it');
	}
	$Info = GetCreditStatus($Order['debtorno']);
	if ($Info !== false AND $Info['status'] == 'stop') {
		return __('This customer is on stop') . ' (' . $Info['reasondescription'] . '). ' . __('The order cannot be dispatched or invoiced until credit control takes the customer off stop or releases this order');
	}
	return '';
}

/* The customer sees a plain message - not the internal reason */
function CCCustomerStopMessage() {
	return __('Your account is on hold. Please contact us to arrange payment before placing further orders');
}

/* The date of the next credit review for a customer opened or reviewed today */
function CCNextReviewDate($Months = 0, $FromDate = '') {
	if ($Months <= 0) {
		$Months = (int)CCSetting('CCReviewMonths', 12);
	}
	if ($Months <= 0) {
		$Months = 12;
	}
	if ($FromDate == '') {
		$FromDate = date('Y-m-d');
	}
	return date('Y-m-d', strtotime($FromDate . ' +' . $Months . ' months'));
}

/* SQL expression for the days an item is overdue. Negative or zero means not yet due. Uses the same rule as AgedDebtors.php:
terms in days run from the transaction date, terms in the following month run from the end of the month plus the day number */
function CCDaysOverdueSQL() {
	return "IF(paymentterms.daysbeforedue > 0,
				TO_DAYS(CURRENT_DATE) - TO_DAYS(debtortrans.trandate) - paymentterms.daysbeforedue,
				TO_DAYS(CURRENT_DATE) - TO_DAYS(ADDDATE(LAST_DAY(debtortrans.trandate), paymentterms.dayinfollowingmonth)))";
}

/* Open invoices and charges of a customer that are overdue by at least $MinDays. Invoices marked disputed are left out.
Returns rows with id, type, transno, trandate, balance, rate, daysoverdue. */
function CCOverdueItems($DebtorNo, $MinDays = 1, $IncludeDisputed = false, $Types = '10,51') {
	$SQL = "SELECT debtortrans.id,
					debtortrans.type,
					debtortrans.transno,
					debtortrans.trandate,
					debtortrans.balance,
					debtortrans.rate,
					debtortrans.reference,
					debtortrans.disputed,
					" . CCDaysOverdueSQL() . " AS daysoverdue
			FROM debtortrans
			INNER JOIN debtorsmaster
				ON debtortrans.debtorno = debtorsmaster.debtorno
			INNER JOIN paymentterms
				ON debtorsmaster.paymentterms = paymentterms.termsindicator
			WHERE debtortrans.debtorno = '" . $DebtorNo . "'
				AND debtortrans.type IN (" . $Types . ")
				AND debtortrans.settled = 0
				AND debtortrans.balance > " . CurrencyTolerance($_SESSION['CompanyRecord']['currencydefault']) . "
				" . ($IncludeDisputed ? '' : 'AND debtortrans.disputed = 0') . "
			HAVING daysoverdue >= " . (int)$MinDays . "
			ORDER BY debtortrans.trandate, debtortrans.id";
	$Result = DB_query($SQL);
	$Items = array();
	while ($Row = DB_fetch_array($Result)) {
		$Items[] = $Row;
	}
	return $Items;
}

/* Local currency value of an amount in the customer's currency. A rate of 0 is never stored by webERP but guard anyway */
function CCToLocal($Amount, $Rate) {
	if ($Rate == 0) {
		$Rate = 1;
	}
	return round($Amount / $Rate, 4);
}

function CCGLEntry($Type, $TransNo, $TranDate, $PeriodNo, $Account, $Narrative, $Amount) {
	$SQL = "INSERT INTO gltrans (type,
								typeno,
								trandate,
								periodno,
								account,
								narrative,
								amount)
					VALUES ('" . $Type . "',
						'" . $TransNo . "',
						'" . $TranDate . "',
						'" . $PeriodNo . "',
						'" . $Account . "',
						'" . DB_escape_string(mb_substr(stripslashes($Narrative), 0, 200)) . "',
						'" . $Amount . "')";
	DB_query($SQL, __('CRITICAL ERROR') . '! ' . __('NOTE DOWN THIS ERROR AND SEEK ASSISTANCE') . ': ' . __('The GL entry for the credit control transaction could not be inserted because'), '', true);
}

/* Inserts a debtortrans row for a charge (type 51, positive) or a credit (types 52 and 53, negative). Returns the new row id.
The branch is the customer's first branch, as for any account level transaction. */
function CCInsertDebtorTrans($Type, $TransNo, $DebtorNo, $TranDate, $PeriodNo, $Rate, $Amount, $Reference, $Text) {
	$BranchResult = DB_query("SELECT branchcode, salesman FROM custbranch WHERE debtorno='" . $DebtorNo . "' ORDER BY branchcode LIMIT 1");
	$Branch = DB_fetch_array($BranchResult);
	$TypeResult = DB_query("SELECT salestype FROM debtorsmaster WHERE debtorno='" . $DebtorNo . "'");
	$Debtor = DB_fetch_array($TypeResult);
	$SQL = "INSERT INTO debtortrans (transno,
									type,
									debtorno,
									branchcode,
									trandate,
									inputdate,
									prd,
									reference,
									tpe,
									rate,
									ovamount,
									invtext,
									salesperson)
				VALUES ('" . $TransNo . "',
						'" . $Type . "',
						'" . $DebtorNo . "',
						'" . $Branch['branchcode'] . "',
						'" . $TranDate . "',
						'" . date('Y-m-d H:i:s') . "',
						'" . $PeriodNo . "',
						'" . DB_escape_string(mb_substr(stripslashes($Reference), 0, 50)) . "',
						'" . $Debtor['salestype'] . "',
						'" . $Rate . "',
						'" . $Amount . "',
						'" . DB_escape_string(stripslashes($Text)) . "',
						'" . $Branch['salesman'] . "')";
	DB_query($SQL, __('CRITICAL ERROR') . '! ' . __('NOTE DOWN THIS ERROR AND SEEK ASSISTANCE') . ': ' . __('The customer transaction could not be inserted because'), '', true);
	return DB_Last_Insert_ID('debtortrans', 'id');
}

/* Allocates a credit (negative debtortrans row, amount in customer currency) to a customer's open items, oldest first, the way the
allocation pages do: custallocns from the credit to each item, alloc and settled updated on both sides.
Returns the list of what was allocated: id, amount, rate. The caller decides what to do with items it did not cover. */
function CCAllocateCredit($CreditID, $DebtorNo, $Amount, $OnlyItemID = 0) {
	$Tolerance = CurrencyTolerance($_SESSION['CompanyRecord']['currencydefault']);
	$SQL = "SELECT id, balance, rate
			FROM debtortrans
			WHERE debtorno = '" . $DebtorNo . "'
				AND type IN (10, 51)
				AND settled = 0
				AND balance > " . $Tolerance . "
				" . ($OnlyItemID > 0 ? "AND id = '" . $OnlyItemID . "'" : '') . "
			ORDER BY trandate, id";
	$Result = DB_query($SQL);
	$Remaining = $Amount;
	$Allocated = array();
	while ($Row = DB_fetch_array($Result) AND $Remaining > $Tolerance / 2) {
		$Take = min($Row['balance'], $Remaining);
		DB_query("INSERT INTO custallocns (datealloc, amt, transid_allocfrom, transid_allocto)
					VALUES (CURRENT_DATE, '" . $Take . "', '" . $CreditID . "', '" . $Row['id'] . "')",
				__('The allocation of the credit could not be recorded because'), '', true);
		$Settled = (abs($Row['balance'] - $Take) < $Tolerance) ? 1 : 0;
		DB_query("UPDATE debtortrans SET alloc = alloc + " . $Take . ", settled = " . $Settled . " WHERE id = '" . $Row['id'] . "'",
				__('The allocated item could not be updated because'), '', true);
		$Allocated[] = array('id' => $Row['id'], 'amount' => $Take, 'rate' => $Row['rate']);
		$Remaining -= $Take;
	}
	$Total = $Amount - $Remaining;
	$Settled = (abs($Remaining) < $Tolerance) ? 1 : 0;
	DB_query("UPDATE debtortrans SET alloc = alloc - " . $Total . ", settled = " . $Settled . " WHERE id = '" . $CreditID . "'",
			__('The credit could not be updated because'), '', true);
	return $Allocated;
}

/* Total of the open invoices and charges that a write-off could be applied to, in the customer's currency */
function CCWriteOffCeiling($DebtorNo) {
	$SQL = "SELECT SUM(balance) AS open
			FROM debtortrans
			WHERE debtorno = '" . $DebtorNo . "'
				AND type IN (10, 51)
				AND settled = 0
				AND balance > 0";
	$MyRow = DB_fetch_array(DB_query($SQL));
	return $MyRow['open'] == '' ? 0 : $MyRow['open'];
}

/* Posts an approved write-off: a type 53 credit, allocated to the oldest open items, bad debt debited and debtors control credited
at the rate each allocated item was originally posted at, so the control account falls by exactly what the items carried.
Must be called inside a transaction. Returns the transaction number. */
function CCPostWriteOff($WriteOffID, $DebtorNo, $Amount, $Reason) {
	$Info = GetCreditStatus($DebtorNo);
	$TranDate = date('Y-m-d');
	$PeriodNo = GetPeriod(date($_SESSION['DefaultDateFormat']));
	$TransNo = GetNextTransNo(53);
	$Rate = ($Info['rate'] == 0) ? 1 : $Info['rate'];
	$CreditID = CCInsertDebtorTrans(53, $TransNo, $DebtorNo, $TranDate, $PeriodNo, $Rate, -$Amount,
		__('Bad debt write-off') . ' ' . $WriteOffID, $Reason);
	$Allocated = CCAllocateCredit($CreditID, $DebtorNo, $Amount);

	$Local = 0;
	$AllocatedFX = 0;
	foreach ($Allocated as $Item) {
		$Local += CCToLocal($Item['amount'], $Item['rate']);
		$AllocatedFX += $Item['amount'];
	}
	/* the write-off row carries the average rate of what it cleared so balance and ledger agree */
	if ($AllocatedFX > 0 AND $Local > 0) {
		DB_query("UPDATE debtortrans SET rate = '" . ($AllocatedFX / $Local) . "' WHERE id = '" . $CreditID . "'");
	}
	if ($_SESSION['CompanyRecord']['gllink_debtors'] == 1 AND $Local != 0) {
		$Narrative = $DebtorNo . ' ' . __('bad debt write-off') . ' ' . $Reason;
		CCGLEntry(53, $TransNo, $TranDate, $PeriodNo, CCSetting('CCBadDebtAct'), $Narrative, $Local);
		CCGLEntry(53, $TransNo, $TranDate, $PeriodNo, $_SESSION['CompanyRecord']['debtorsact'], $Narrative, -$Local);
		EnsureGLEntriesBalance(53, $TransNo);
	}
	return $TransNo;
}

/* Customer contacts the reminder letters go to: the contacts flagged to receive statements, the accounts contacts, with a valid email */
function CCAccountsEmails($DebtorNo) {
	$Result = DB_query("SELECT email FROM custcontacts WHERE debtorno='" . $DebtorNo . "' AND statement=1");
	$Emails = array();
	while ($Row = DB_fetch_row($Result)) {
		if (IsEmailAddress($Row[0]) AND !in_array($Row[0], $Emails)) {
			$Emails[] = $Row[0];
		}
	}
	return $Emails;
}

/* A sales rep only sees credit information for their own customers. SalesmanLogin is set for rep logins by session.php.
Returns true when the logged in user may see the customer. */
function CCUserMaySeeCustomer($DebtorNo) {
	if (!isset($_SESSION['SalesmanLogin']) OR $_SESSION['SalesmanLogin'] == '') {
		return true;
	}
	$Result = DB_query("SELECT debtorno FROM custbranch WHERE debtorno='" . $DebtorNo . "' AND salesman='" . $_SESSION['SalesmanLogin'] . "' LIMIT 1");
	return DB_num_rows($Result) > 0;
}

/* Banner used on the pages where staff look at a customer or take an order for them */
function CCStatusBanner($DebtorNo) {
	$Info = GetCreditStatus($DebtorNo);
	if ($Info === false OR $Info['status'] == 'normal') {
		return '';
	}
	$Class = ($Info['status'] == 'stop') ? 'error' : 'warn';
	return prnMsg(CCStatusName($Info['status']) . ' - ' . $Info['reasondescription'] . '. ' . __('Credit limit') . ' ' . locale_number_format($Info['creditlimit'], 2) . ' ' . $Info['currcode'], $Class, '', true);
}

# Credit control - developer notes

Nothing here has been run: there was no database or web server to run against. The PHP, SQL and the upgrade file are written to the project's patterns
and checked by reading, not by executing. Run the upgrade on a copy of the live database and walk AC-01 to AC-12 before this goes near production.

## The main design decision: build on the hold reason, do not add a second status

webERP already has a stop and a watch. `debtorsmaster.holdreason` points to `holdreasons`, and `holdreasons.dissallowinvoices` is 1 for stop and 2 for watch.
`SelectOrderItems.php`, `CounterSales.php`, `SpecialOrder.php`, the aged debtors "held only" option and the account inquiry already read it. A new status column would have
left two sources of truth and the existing "stop list" (customers already on a stopping hold reason) would not have carried over on its own. So:

- Credit status = the customer's hold reason (stop / watch / normal). `GetCreditStatus()` in `includes/CreditControlFunctions.php` is the one reader.
- On go-live everything on a stopping hold reason today is already on stop (BR-40); the upgrade does not touch `holdreason`.
- Three hold reasons are added (90 normal, 91 watch, 92 stop) so the credit control page always has a reason of each kind to use.

## What was built

| Need | Where |
|---|---|
| Reviews, stop/watch changes, limit changes, disputed invoices, exemptions, collection-agency note, per-customer history (BR-01..05, 08, 09, 18, 20, 32) | `CreditControl.php` |
| Report: reviews due, over limit (total in home currency), watch, stop, orders held or taken for watched/stopped customers, release of held orders; rep and currency filters (BR-30, 33) | `CreditControlReport.php` |
| Finance settings: review period, interest rate, fee, days before charging, GL accounts, write-off limit, switches (BR-02, 12, 19, 23, 26) | `CreditControlSetup.php`, `DunningStages.php` |
| Reminder run: preview, leave customers out, email, post list for no-email customers, log (BR-12..17) | `DunningRun.php` |
| Month end interest and fees: preview, confirm, post to GL, once per month, waiver (BR-19..24) | `CreditCharges.php` |
| Bad debt write-off, Finance Director approval, auto stop, report (BR-25..29) | `CreditWriteOff.php`, `CreditWriteOffReport.php` |
| Customer view of reminders and charges (BR-35, 36) | `CustomerCreditPortal.php`, link added in the customer menu in `index.php` |
| Month end agreement GL to customer accounts, with the transactions that differ (BR-37, 38) | `DebtorsReconciliation.php` |
| Shared code | `includes/CreditControlFunctions.php` |
| Staff guide (BR-42, 43) | `doc/Manual/ManualAccountsReceivable.html`, section "Credit Control" (includes the short note for sales staff) |

### Schema (a new numbered update and the install files - both, because the numbered runner never runs on a fresh install)

- `sql/updates/44.php`, with matching `install/sql/tables/*.sql`, `install/sql/data/*.sql` and `install/sql/demo.sql` (the demo install sets `DBUpdateNumber` to the highest
  update, so 44 never runs there; its rows had to be added to `demo.sql` too).
- New tables: `creditreviews`, `creditcontrollog` (history, append only), `dunningstages`, `dunninglog`, `creditcharges`, `creditwriteoffs`.
- New columns: `debtorsmaster.nextreviewdate / reviewmonths / exemptinterest / exemptfees`, `debtortrans.disputed`, `salesorders.creditheld`.
- Existing customers: `nextreviewdate` is spread over the review period (hash of the customer code) rather than all on one day, so Maria is not handed 900 reviews at once.
  Finance can overwrite dates afterwards. Status and limits are untouched.
- Transaction types 51 interest/fee charge, 52 charge waiver, 53 bad debt write-off in `systypes`.
- Security tokens 21 (credit control) and 22 (Finance Director approval of write-offs). The install gives them to the administrator role only; other roles are
  granted them from the security roles page. `CreditControl.php` is registered at token 2 so reps can look; changing anything checks token 21 inside the page.
- Menu rows are added for all nine seeded roles, as the existing seed does.

### Enforcement - every route to an order or an invoice

- `DeliveryDetails.php` is the last gate for sales office and web shop orders (and quotation-to-order conversion): stop = refused, over limit = saved with `creditheld = 1`,
  watch = accepted with a warning.
- `SelectOrderItems.php`: a customer login on watch was being told its account was on hold and refused (the test was `dissallowinvoices == 0`). Only stop (1) refuses now.
  The stop message for web shop customers is plain (BR-11) and does not give the internal reason.
- `EDIProcessOrders.php`: stop = no order, error mail text; over limit = order created and held.
  This needed a bug fix: `if ($CreateOrder = true)` assigned instead of compared, so nothing could ever stop an EDI order. It is now `==`. Side effect: message functions
  16/31/42/46 and unmatched customers no longer create an order, which is what the code's own comments say it should do.
- `RecurringSalesOrdersProcess.php`: stop = template skipped and stays due; over limit = order raised, held, and not auto-invoiced.
- API (`api_salesorders.php`): header insert refused for stop (new error codes 1174/1175); `InvoiceSalesOrder` refuses stopped customers and held orders and holds an unchecked
  order that is over the limit (the API builds orders line by line, so the value is only known at invoicing).
- `ConfirmDispatch_Invoice.php`: nothing is dispatched or invoiced for a customer on stop or for a held order unless that order was released (`creditheld = 2`).
  Orders taken before a stop are therefore blocked until credit control releases them from the credit control report (BR-06).
- Counter sales already refused stopped customers.
- `Customers.php`: credit limit and hold reason are only changeable by token 21. Everyone else keeps the stored values (with a warning) and new customers start on the default
  limit and a normal reason (BR-07, 34). Changes by credit control through that page are written to the history. A customer with a history cannot be deleted.
  New customers get a next review date (also in the API `InsertCustomer` and `Z_ImportDebtors.php`).
- `Z_ChangeCustomerCode.php` copies the new columns and moves the history tables to the new code (otherwise the foreign keys would block the rename).

### Postings

- Interest and fees: one `debtortrans` type 51 per customer per month per kind (so they show separately on the account and the statement, which already lists
  outstanding items with the `systypes` name). GL: debtors control debit, Finance's income account credit. Unique key (customer, month, kind) is the double-charge guard,
  and the post recomputes everything from the database rather than trusting the preview.
- Waiver: type 52 credit allocated to the charge, GL reversed at the charge's rate. For a part-paid charge only the outstanding part is waived.
- Write-off: type 53 credit allocated oldest-first to open invoices/charges (`custallocns`, `alloc`, `settled`, like the allocation pages). Debtors control is credited at the
  rate each cleared item was originally posted at, so the control account falls by exactly what the items carried and the currency difference lands in bad debt (BR-27).

## Decisions on the open questions

1. Interest: a simple annual rate (company-wide), applied pro rata for the days in the month. Not by currency or country - not enough information, easy to extend.
2. Late fee: one flat fee per customer per month, set in the company currency and converted at the customer's rate.
3. No interest on interest and fees by default (switch in the setup page).
4. After the final notice the customer is flagged for Maria, not stopped automatically. The reminder results page links to the credit page.
5. Over-limit orders from any route, including the web shop and standing orders, are saved and held for approval, not rejected. Note: system parameter
   "Check Credit Limits = Prohibit sales" (2) still blocks at line entry, before an order exists. Use "Warn" (1) with the hold switched on to get the approval workflow.
6. Write-off approval limit is a setting (default 1000 in company currency) - Finance must set it. The Financial Accountant does not sign off; only the Finance Director
   (token 22) can approve. Nothing stops the same person requesting and approving if they hold both tokens.
7. A receipt after a write-off is entered as a normal receipt. The write-off report shows what has been paid since; the accountant journals the recovery. No automatic reversal.
8. Reps see the hold reason description (e.g. "Credit Control - Stop"), not the internal log notes.
9. Letters are one language per stage (the wording is editable). Per-language wording is not built.
10. Customers never see watch status. They see a stop only as "your account is on hold, please contact us".
11. Cover when both Maria and the deputy are away: the token model covers it - any user granted token 21 acts, the Finance Director has both tokens. Not a software question.
12. The limit is per customer (debtor), so all branches share one limit, because that is how webERP holds it. Separate head-office/branch groups would need a new group concept.

Other choices: reminders go to the customer's contacts flagged to receive statements (the existing accounts-contact flag); minimum 14 days between letters and no repeat of the
same stage within 90 days; disputed invoices and invoices not yet overdue never count.

## Known gaps and things to check

- The reminder email is plain text. Text typed into forms has already been HTML-encoded by `session.php`; the code decodes it for the letter.
- Changing a customer's limit or hold reason through the XML-RPC API (`ModifyCustomer`) is not restricted or logged - API users are trusted integrations. Worth deciding.
- Other places that write `debtorsmaster` or take orders and were not changed: counter returns, special orders (stop already refused there), `Z_DeleteInvoice` utilities.
- `DebtorsReconciliation.php` compares at transaction rates; exchange differences posted by allocations show up in its second list as postings with no customer transaction.
  Revaluation journals, if used, will also appear there.
- `CheckCreditLimits`, `PastDueDays1/2` and payment terms drive "overdue"; the days-overdue rule is the one `AgedDebtors.php` uses.
- No automated tests exist in the repository for these pages.

Nothing here has been run: there was no database or web server to run against. The PHP, SQL and the upgrade file are written to the project's patterns
and checked by reading, not by executing. Run the upgrade on a copy of the live database and walk AC-01 to AC-12 before this goes near production.

## The main design decision: build on the hold reason, do not add a second status

webERP already has a stop and a watch. `debtorsmaster.holdreason` points to `holdreasons`, and `holdreasons.dissallowinvoices` is 1 for stop and 2 for watch.
`SelectOrderItems.php`, `CounterSales.php`, `SpecialOrder.php`, the aged debtors "held only" option and the account inquiry already read it. A new status column would have
left two sources of truth and the existing "stop list" (customers already on a stopping hold reason) would not have carried over on its own. So:

- Credit status = the customer's hold reason (stop / watch / normal). `GetCreditStatus()` in `includes/CreditControlFunctions.php` is the one reader.
- On go-live everything on a stopping hold reason today is already on stop (BR-40); the upgrade does not touch `holdreason`.
- Three hold reasons are added (90 normal, 91 watch, 92 stop) so the credit control page always has a reason of each kind to use.

## What was built

| Need | Where |
|---|---|
| Reviews, stop/watch changes, limit changes, disputed invoices, exemptions, collection-agency note, per-customer history (BR-01..05, 08, 09, 18, 20, 32) | `CreditControl.php` |
| Report: reviews due, over limit (total in home currency), watch, stop, orders held or taken for watched/stopped customers, release of held orders; rep and currency filters (BR-30, 33) | `CreditControlReport.php` |
| Finance settings: review period, interest rate, fee, days before charging, GL accounts, write-off limit, switches (BR-02, 12, 19, 23, 26) | `CreditControlSetup.php`, `DunningStages.php` |
| Reminder run: preview, leave customers out, email, post list for no-email customers, log (BR-12..17) | `DunningRun.php` |
| Month end interest and fees: preview, confirm, post to GL, once per month, waiver (BR-19..24) | `CreditCharges.php` |
| Bad debt write-off, Finance Director approval, auto stop, report (BR-25..29) | `CreditWriteOff.php`, `CreditWriteOffReport.php` |
| Customer view of reminders and charges (BR-35, 36) | `CustomerCreditPortal.php`, link added in the customer menu in `index.php` |
| Month end agreement GL to customer accounts, with the transactions that differ (BR-37, 38) | `DebtorsReconciliation.php` |
| Shared code | `includes/CreditControlFunctions.php` |
| Staff guide (BR-42, 43) | `doc/Manual/ManualAccountsReceivable.html`, section "Credit Control" (includes the short note for sales staff) |

### Schema (a new numbered update and the install files - both, because the numbered runner never runs on a fresh install)

- `sql/updates/44.php`, with matching `install/sql/tables/*.sql`, `install/sql/data/*.sql` and `install/sql/demo.sql` (the demo install sets `DBUpdateNumber` to the highest
  update, so 44 never runs there; its rows had to be added to `demo.sql` too).
- New tables: `creditreviews`, `creditcontrollog` (history, append only), `dunningstages`, `dunninglog`, `creditcharges`, `creditwriteoffs`.
- New columns: `debtorsmaster.nextreviewdate / reviewmonths / exemptinterest / exemptfees`, `debtortrans.disputed`, `salesorders.creditheld`.
- Existing customers: `nextreviewdate` is spread over the review period (hash of the customer code) rather than all on one day, so Maria is not handed 900 reviews at once.
  Finance can overwrite dates afterwards. Status and limits are untouched.
- Transaction types 51 interest/fee charge, 52 charge waiver, 53 bad debt write-off in `systypes`.
- Security tokens 21 (credit control) and 22 (Finance Director approval of write-offs). The install gives them to the administrator role only; other roles are
  granted them from the security roles page. `CreditControl.php` is registered at token 2 so reps can look; changing anything checks token 21 inside the page.
- Menu rows are added for all nine seeded roles, as the existing seed does.

### Enforcement - every route to an order or an invoice

- `DeliveryDetails.php` is the last gate for sales office and web shop orders (and quotation-to-order conversion): stop = refused, over limit = saved with `creditheld = 1`,
  watch = accepted with a warning.
- `SelectOrderItems.php`: a customer login on watch was being told its account was on hold and refused (the test was `dissallowinvoices == 0`). Only stop (1) refuses now.
  The stop message for web shop customers is plain (BR-11) and does not give the internal reason.
- `EDIProcessOrders.php`: stop = no order, error mail text; over limit = order created and held.
  This needed a bug fix: `if ($CreateOrder = true)` assigned instead of compared, so nothing could ever stop an EDI order. It is now `==`. Side effect: message functions
  16/31/42/46 and unmatched customers no longer create an order, which is what the code's own comments say it should do.
- `RecurringSalesOrdersProcess.php`: stop = template skipped and stays due; over limit = order raised, held, and not auto-invoiced.
- API (`api_salesorders.php`): header insert refused for stop (new error codes 1174/1175); `InvoiceSalesOrder` refuses stopped customers and held orders and holds an unchecked
  order that is over the limit (the API builds orders line by line, so the value is only known at invoicing).
- `ConfirmDispatch_Invoice.php`: nothing is dispatched or invoiced for a customer on stop or for a held order unless that order was released (`creditheld = 2`).
  Orders taken before a stop are therefore blocked until credit control releases them from the credit control report (BR-06).
- Counter sales already refused stopped customers.
- `Customers.php`: credit limit and hold reason are only changeable by token 21. Everyone else keeps the stored values (with a warning) and new customers start on the default
  limit and a normal reason (BR-07, 34). Changes by credit control through that page are written to the history. A customer with a history cannot be deleted.
  New customers get a next review date (also in the API `InsertCustomer` and `Z_ImportDebtors.php`).
- `Z_ChangeCustomerCode.php` copies the new columns and moves the history tables to the new code (otherwise the foreign keys would block the rename).

### Postings

- Interest and fees: one `debtortrans` type 51 per customer per month per kind (so they show separately on the account and the statement, which already lists
  outstanding items with the `systypes` name). GL: debtors control debit, Finance's income account credit. Unique key (customer, month, kind) is the double-charge guard,
  and the post recomputes everything from the database rather than trusting the preview.
- Waiver: type 52 credit allocated to the charge, GL reversed at the charge's rate. For a part-paid charge only the outstanding part is waived.
- Write-off: type 53 credit allocated oldest-first to open invoices/charges (`custallocns`, `alloc`, `settled`, like the allocation pages). Debtors control is credited at the
  rate each cleared item was originally posted at, so the control account falls by exactly what the items carried and the currency difference lands in bad debt (BR-27).

2. Late fee: one flat fee per customer per month, set in the company currency and converted at the customer's rate.
3. No interest on interest and fees by default (switch in the setup page).
4. After the final notice the customer is flagged for Maria, not stopped automatically. The reminder results page links to the credit page.

9. Letters are one language per stage (the wording is editable). Per-language wording is not built.
10. Customers never see watch status. They see a stop only as "your account is on hold, please contact us".
11. Cover when both Maria and the deputy are away: the token model covers it - any user granted token 21 acts, the Finance Director has both tokens. Not a software question.
12. The limit is per customer (debtor), so all branches share one limit, because that is how webERP holds it. Separate head-office/branch groups would need a new group concept.

Other choices: reminders go to the customer's contacts flagged to receive statements (the existing accounts-contact flag); minimum 14 days between letters and no repeat of the
same stage within 90 days; disputed invoices and invoices not yet overdue never count.

## Known gaps and things to check

- The reminder email is plain text. Text typed into forms has already been HTML-encoded by `session.php`; the code decodes it for the letter.
- Changing a customer's limit or hold reason through the XML-RPC API (`ModifyCustomer`) is not restricted or logged - API users are trusted integrations. Worth deciding.
